question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

23, 70, 212, 637, 1913, ? , 17222
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 5740.

GIVEN

• 23, 70, 212, 637, 1913, ? , 17222

SOLUTION

• The pattern is alternately ×3+1 and ×3+2.

• 23×3+1 = 70; 70×3+2 = 212; 212×3+1 = 637; 637×3+2 = 1913.

• Next term = 1913×3+1 = 5739+1 = 5740.

• Check: 5740×3+2 = 17220+2 = 17222 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Multiply each term by 3 and add 1, 2, 1, 2 … alternately; 1913×3+1 = 5740.

NOTE

• In fast-growing series, first test ×3 (or ×2, ×4) and read off the small alternating add-on (+1/+2).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

C, H, N, U, ?, L, V, G
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. C.

GIVEN

• C, H, N, U, ?, L, V, G

SOLUTION

• Positions: C=3, H=8, N=14, U=21 with gaps +5, +6, +7.

• Next gap +8: 21+8 = 29 → 29−26 = 3 = C.

• Continue: C(3)+9 = 12 = L; L+10 = 22 = V; V(22)+11 = 33−26 = 7 = G ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Gaps increase 5, 6, 7, 8, 9…; add 8 to U (21) and wrap past Z to get C.

NOTE

• Use A=1…Z=26 and subtract 26 whenever the count crosses Z.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

ID, GC, EA, CX, AT, YO, WI, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. UB.

GIVEN

• ID, GC, EA, CX, AT, YO, WI, ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: I, G, E, C, A, Y, W, ? decrease by 2 → W(23)−2 = 21 = U.

• 2nd letters: D, C, A, X, T, O, I, ? decrease by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 → I(9)−7 = 2 = B.

• So the missing cluster = UB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter −2 each step, second letter decreasing gaps (−1,−2,…,−7); apply to WI.

NOTE

• Split a two-letter series into two independent letter series and track each with position numbers.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and third letter cluster is related to fourth letter cluster.

AX : VQ :: TN : OG :: ? : CB
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. HI.

GIVEN

• AX : VQ :: TN : OG :: ? : CB

SOLUTION

• Rule: 1st letter −5, 2nd letter −7. Check AX: A(1)−5=22=V, X(24)−7=17=Q ✓; TN: T(20)−5=15=O, N(14)−7=7=G ✓.

• Given the second cluster CB, reverse the rule: C(3)+5 = 8 = H, B(2)+7 = 9 = I.

• So ? = HI.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Answer = C+5, B+7 = H, I → HI.

NOTE

• When the missing cluster is the FIRST of a pair, add back the shift (reverse the mapping).

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(NK, LI, OR)

(CP, AN, ZM)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (LN, JL, QO).

GIVEN

• Sets: (NK, LI, OR) and (CP, AN, ZM)

SOLUTION

• In each set all three clusters share the SAME letter-gap magnitude, with two clusters one sign and the third the opposite sign.

• (NK, LI, OR): gaps −3, −3, +3; (CP, AN, ZM): gaps +13, +13, −13.

• Option 3 (LN, JL, QO): L→N +2, J→L +2, Q→O −2 — same magnitude (2, 2, 2) with the ++− pattern ✓.

• Other options give mixed magnitudes, so they fail.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the internal letter-gap of each cluster; the valid group has equal gaps with a two-same-one-opposite sign pattern.

NOTE

• For odd-set classification, compare the RULE among clusters, not the letters themselves.

question: What will be the product of the number of Sundays and Fridays in the month of February in the year 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 16.

GIVEN

• Month = February 2020 (leap year, 29 days).

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2020 was Wednesday; Jan has 31 days, so 1 Feb 2020 = Wednesday+3 = Saturday.

• 29 days = 4 weeks + 1 extra day; the extra day (1 Feb = Sat) makes Saturday occur 5 times, all other days 4 times.

• So Sundays = 4 and Fridays = 4 → product = 4×4 = 16.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 29-day month = one weekday appears 5 times (the starting day); all others appear 4 times.

NOTE

• Feb 2020 starts on Saturday; only Saturday repeats 5 times.

question: What was the last day of the year 1889?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Tuesday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 31 December 1889.

SOLUTION

• Odd days in 1888 complete years: 1600 → 0; 288 years (200 → 3, 88 → 5) = 8 → 1 odd day.

• Add full year 1889 up to 31 Dec = 365 days = 1 odd day.

• Total odd days = 1 + 1 = 2 → Sunday+2 = Tuesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Last day of a year = same day as 31 Dec; total odd days 2 ⇒ Tuesday.

NOTE

• Odd-day counts: 100 yrs = 5, 200 = 3, 300 = 1, 400 = 0; a non-leap year adds 1 odd day.

question: 5 teachers P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). P is third to the right of T. S is fourth to the right of T. Q is second to the right of T. What is the position of R from the right end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Fourth.

GIVEN

• P = 3rd right of T, S = 4th right of T, Q = 2nd right of T.

SOLUTION

• Place T first; going rightward: T, _, Q(2nd), P(3rd), S(4th).

• The blank (1st right of T) is the only person left = R.

• Order in the right direction: T, R, Q, P, S.

• From the right end: S(1), P(2), Q(3), R(4), T(5).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Fit the ‘nth to the right’ clues into 5 seats; R fills the only gap and lands 4th from the right end.

NOTE

• ‘From the right end’ is counted along the same right-direction as the clues, so facing direction does not change the count here.

question: Price of 6 bags B, C, D, E, F and G is compared. Price of no two bags is same. Number of bags having price less than B are 'X – 2'. Number of bags having price more than D are 'X'. Price of E is third lowest. Price of C is less than F but more than G. Price of D is not lowest. Price of how many bags is more than the price of bag G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• 6 bags; less-than-B = X−2; more-than-D = X; E third lowest; G < C < F; D not lowest.

SOLUTION

• Try X = 2: bags less than B = 0 ⇒ B is lowest; bags more than D = 2 ⇒ D is 4th from bottom.

• Placing E as 3rd lowest and keeping G < C < F: order (low→high) = B, G, E, D, C, F.

• All conditions check: E 3rd lowest ✓, C<F ✓, C>G ✓, D not lowest ✓.

• Bags priced more than G = E, D, C, F = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Test X = 2 → B lowest, D 4th; G sits 2nd from bottom, so 4 bags beat G.

NOTE

• In ranking puzzles, convert ‘number less/more than’ statements directly into rank positions.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LP40 : PT160 :: ? : KN220 :: TJ310 : XN430
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. GJ100.

GIVEN

• LP40 : PT160 :: ? : KN220 :: TJ310 : XN430

SOLUTION

• Rule: both letters +4, number +120. Check LP40→PT160: L+4=P, P+4=T, 40+120=160 ✓; TJ310→XN430: T+4=X, J+4=N, 310+120=430 ✓.

• Given the second cluster KN220, reverse: K−4 = G, N−4 = J, 220−120 = 100.

• So ? = GJ100.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 4 from each letter and 120 from the number of KN220 → GJ100.

NOTE

• When the unknown is the FIRST cluster of a pair, apply the inverse of the forward rule.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AC120 : GL295 :: DK230 : ? :: LO320 : RX495
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. JT405.

GIVEN

• AC120 : GL295 :: DK230 : ? :: LO320 : RX495

SOLUTION

• Rule: 1st letter +6, 2nd letter +9, number +175. Check AC120→GL295: A+6=G, C+9=L, 120+175=295 ✓; LO320→RX495: L+6=R, O+9=X, 320+175=495 ✓.

• Apply to DK230: D+6 = J, K+9 = T, 230+175 = 405.

• So ? = JT405.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• +6, +9 on letters and +175 on the number of DK230 → JT405.

NOTE

• Fix the letter-shift and the constant number-add from one solved pair, then apply forward.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to fourth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

9452 : 9404 :: 5963 : 5915 :: ? : 3769
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3817.

GIVEN

• 9452 : 9404 :: 5963 : 5915 :: ? : 3769

SOLUTION

• Rule: first number − 48 = second. Check 9452−48 = 9404 ✓; 5963−48 = 5915 ✓.

• Here 3769 is the SECOND number, so first = 3769 + 48 = 3817.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Each pair differs by 48; add 48 back to 3769 → 3817.

NOTE

• Find the constant difference from a solved pair, then reverse it for the unknown first term.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

610 : 1837 :: ? : 1456 :: 793 : 2386
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 483.

GIVEN

• 610 : 1837 :: ? : 1456 :: 793 : 2386

SOLUTION

• Rule: first ×3 + 7 = second. Check 610×3+7 = 1837 ✓; 793×3+7 = 2386 ✓.

• Here 1456 is the second number, so first ×3 = 1456 − 7 = 1449 → first = 1449 ÷ 3 = 483.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse ×3+7: (1456 − 7) ÷ 3 = 483.

NOTE

• Detect the ‘×k + c’ rule from a solved pair, then invert it to recover the missing first term.

question: In a certain code language, 'TREE' is coded as '16' and 'TRUNK' is coded as '28'. How will 'MONEY' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 24.

GIVEN

• TREE = 16, TRUNK = 28.

SOLUTION

• Rule: (sum of letter positions) ÷ 3.

• TREE = 20+18+5+5 = 48; 48÷3 = 16 ✓. TRUNK = 20+18+21+14+11 = 84; 84÷3 = 28 ✓.

• MONEY = 13+15+14+5+25 = 72; 72÷3 = 24.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all letter positions and divide by 3 → 72 ÷ 3 = 24.

NOTE

• For number-code words, first test the sum of A=1…Z=26 positions, then look for ×/÷ scaling.

question: In a certain code language, 'boys goes for vacation' is coded as 'pl ta pq st', 'vacation relax mood' is coded as 'pq rm op', and 'mood need time' is coded as 'rm td ht'. How will 'vacation mood' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pq rm.

GIVEN

• 'boys goes for vacation' = 'pl ta pq st'; 'vacation relax mood' = 'pq rm op'; 'mood need time' = 'rm td ht'.

SOLUTION

• 'vacation' is common to lines 1 and 2 → common code pq.

• 'mood' is common to lines 2 and 3 → common code rm.

• So 'vacation mood' = pq rm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the word shared by two sentences to the code shared by those sentences.

NOTE

• In word-code problems, intersect the sentences to pin down each word’s code.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

MP48, NT60, OX72, PB84, QF96, SK108
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. SK108.

GIVEN

• MP48, NT60, OX72, PB84, QF96, SK108

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: M, N, O, P, Q, … so the 6th should be R (not S).

• 2nd letters: P, T, X, B, F, … each +4, so the 6th should be J (not K).

• Numbers +12: 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108 ✓. Correct 6th term = RJ108.

• Hence the wrong term is SK108.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters run consecutively and second letters jump +4; the printed SK108 breaks both.

NOTE

• Check each component (letter1, letter2, number) as its own progression to spot the odd term.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

BFY700, CEZ527, DDA354, ?, FBC8
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ECB181.

GIVEN

• BFY700, CEZ527, DDA354, ?, FBC8

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: B, C, D, ?, F → E.

• 2nd letters: F, E, D, ?, B → C.

• 3rd letters: Y, Z, A, ?, C → B.

• Numbers: 700, 527, 354, ?, 8 decrease by 173 each → 354 − 173 = 181.

• So ? = ECB181.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters step E/C/B and number drops 173 each time → ECB181.

NOTE

• Treat each letter column and the number as separate arithmetic progressions.

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) for the first time after 10:00 PM minute hand and hour hand of the clock will make an angle of 15 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 10:52.

GIVEN

• Find the first time after 10:00 PM when the hands are 15° apart.

SOLUTION

• Angle at 10:M = |30×10 − 5.5M| = |300 − 5.5M|.

• Set 300 − 5.5M = 15 → 5.5M = 285 → M = 51.8 ≈ 52.

• So the first time is about 10:52 PM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Use angle = |30H − 5.5M|; solve 300 − 5.5M = 15 → M ≈ 52.

NOTE

• The minute hand moves 5.5° per minute relative to the hour hand.

question: Difference between the present ages of A and B is 2 years. 5 years ago from present, the ratio of ages of A and B is 4 : 3. What is the present age of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 11 years.

GIVEN

• Present |A − B| = 2; 5 years ago A : B = 4 : 3.

SOLUTION

• Let 5 years ago A = 4k, B = 3k. Their difference 4k − 3k = k, which equals the (constant) present difference = 2, so k = 2.

• 5 years ago B = 3k = 6 → present B = 6 + 5 = 11 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Age difference is constant: 1 part = 2, so B = 3×2 + 5 = 11.

NOTE

• The difference of ages never changes with time, so equate it to the ratio-difference.

question: Sum of the present ages of A, B and C is 96 years. 12 years ago from the present the ratio of ages of A, B and C was 1 : 2 : 3. What is the sum of present ages of A and C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 64 years.

GIVEN

• A + B + C = 96 now; 12 years ago A : B : C = 1 : 2 : 3.

SOLUTION

• 12 years ago total = 96 − 3×12 = 60; ratio parts = 1+2+3 = 6, so 1 part = 10.

• Then A = 10, B = 20, C = 30 (12 yrs ago) → present A = 22, B = 32, C = 42.

• Sum of present A and C = 22 + 42 = 64 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Past total 60 → parts of 10; A+C = (1+3)×10 + 2×12 = 40 + 24 = 64.

NOTE

• Subtract n×(number of people) years to shift the total back n years, then split by ratio.
